## What's new in v2.6.2

### Dictation output language: speak one language, paste another (#3181, #4781)

- **New setting:** In `Settings > AI Polish`, with Claude selected, `Dictation output language` writes new dictations in `English`, `German` or `Hindi`. The default is `Same as spoken`, so nothing changes until you pick a language.
- **Short and failed takes:** Very short dictations (3 words or fewer, or a few characters in languages written without spaces) skip AI Polish and stay in the language you spoke. A failed translation keeps your original-language text; after a normal paste, the pill can say `Couldn’t translate. Your original-language text was kept.`
- **Privacy:** Translation is part of Claude AI Polish: your dictation text, and the app name and your custom words when available, go directly to Anthropic under your own key, as AI Polish already does. Your audio stays on your Mac.

### EnviousWispr in French and Spanish (#3142, #4797, #4818, #4821)

- **Two new interface languages:** Menus, settings and messages now come in English, German, Spanish and French. Choose `Français` or `Español` in `Settings > App Settings > Appearance > Language`, then `Relaunch to apply`. `System default` follows your Mac's language.

### Save audio and Show in Finder in History (#4799, #4812, #5001, #5008)

- **Save audio…:** Click `···` on a dictation card, or on a meeting card or meeting page, and choose `Save audio…` when it appears in the menu, to save the recording as an M4A file where you choose. EnviousWispr then shows it in Finder. A meeting's file contains what was recorded, your microphone and the call sound when it was captured, as you hear it in playback. The saved file is your own copy and is not removed when you delete the dictation or its recording.
- **Show in Finder:** For an imported transcript whose original file can be played, `···` > `Show in Finder` reveals the original file. `Locate original…` still finds a moved original.
- **Save names:** `Save as…` and `Save audio…` on a dictation now suggest the app and the date and time with seconds, like `Claude 2026-11-26 at 1.23.50 PM` (or `Dictation …` when the app is unknown), so saves in one folder are easy to tell apart. Meetings and transcripts keep their titles.

### Self-Learning Dictionary: separate switches and a Blocked words list (#3294, #4768, #5006, #5020)

- **Two switches:** `Settings > Dictionary > Learn from...` now has `Learn new words` (learns from your corrections) and `Fix words it learned` (applies learned corrections to new recordings and imports, on by default). With `Fix words it learned` off, words you added yourself still work. With `Enable Dictionary` off, `Fix words it learned` shows `Paused` and `Dictionary is off in Your Words.`
- **Tighter card:** Each line shows a short status word (`Ready`, `Off`, `Paused`, `Not ready`, `Not available`). A state you must act on keeps its button on the line; other reasons and `Learn more` are inside the `?`.
- **Blocked words:** When the learning memory holds something, a `Learning memory` row shows `N blocked`. It opens a `Blocked words` window that lists each blocked fix as heard and fixed, with `Search blocked words`, `Remove` with `Undo`, and `Forget all` with a confirmation. Blocked words stay on your Mac.

### A silent microphone no longer ends a dictation (#4841, #4877)

- **Keeps recording:** A connected microphone that sends only digital silence no longer ends the take. The pill shows `We’re not hearing anything from your microphone.` after 5 seconds of digital silence mid-take (6 seconds when silent since the start), and `Your microphone isn’t sending sound. Stop and check it in Settings.` after 15 seconds. Words said during the silence are not captured.
- **Settings:** `Stop recording on silence` still ends a take after your chosen pause length. Turn the notice off with `Warn when the microphone is silent` (on by default) in `Settings > Dictation Settings > Microphone`. A disconnected microphone, or a recording that receives no audio at all, can still end the take with its own message.

### Clipboard-only dictation (#4479, #4775)

- **Paste dictations automatically:** A new switch in `Settings > Dictation Settings > Clipboard`, on by default. Turn it off and each dictation goes to your clipboard for you to paste with Cmd+V, instead of being pasted for you.

### Setup: Skip ahead while AI polish downloads (#4845, #4864, #4912)

- **Skip ahead:** On Setup's `Almost ready` screen, when the AI polish download is estimated to take more than a minute, or a minute has passed, `This download is taking longer than expected.` offers `Skip ahead` and `Keep waiting`. `Rather not wait? Skip ahead` stays available after `Keep waiting`.
- **Practice without AI polish:** After Skip ahead, the practice box shows `Basic cleanup for now` (filler words and formatting only). AI polish keeps downloading while EnviousWispr is open and turns on by itself when it is ready. After Setup, EnviousWispr can show an `AI polish download complete` pill once the selected model is ready.
- **Menu bar:** The menu shows `AI polish downloading · NN%`. After a quit, a download with saved progress shows `AI polish download paused · Resume`; if nothing was saved yet, start the download again in `Settings > AI Polish`.

### EnviousMeet

- **Custom Words in finished transcripts (#4429, #4767):** Finished meeting transcripts use your Custom Words. A new meeting uses the words saved when it started; `Transcribe again with` uses the words saved when you click it.
- **Smaller meeting audio (#3147, #4887):** EnviousWispr compacts finished meeting audio in the background, checks the smaller copy, and only then removes the full-size recorder files, including for meetings recorded since v2.6.0. Playback, `Save audio…`, `Transcribe again with` and the transcript work from the smaller copy. There is no setting.
- **Speaker labels (#4936, #4985, #4990, #4957, #4940, #4944, #4946, #4950):** The Speaker labels download has two parts of about 199 MB each, for live labels and for finished calls. With EnviousMeet set up and the live part ready, if the finished-calls part is missing after an update, EnviousWispr can download it by itself when EnviousMeet is idle, and never starts while a meeting records or is transcribed; `Cancel` or `Remove` on `EnviousMeet > Models` stops that until you press `Download`. Voice grouping is better, and speaker names are found again in Zoom 7.2.5 and the Teams app. Cancel now stops a Speaker labels download promptly.
- **More meeting fixes:** A Meet call in Dia is detected as Dia (#4844); summary engine limits are explained with a way to choose another engine (#4790); a summary waiting its turn says so (#4874); automatic transcription recovery is capped (#4762); fewer false Live Preview audio drop warnings (#4764); a local Ollama summary model is unloaded when no summary work needs it (#4856); the EnviousMeet logo stops moving after two waves (#5012).

### Free memory from the on-Mac polish model (#3853, #4867, #4875, #4904)

- **Unload polish model after:** With EG-1 or S1-mini, `Settings > AI Polish` offers `Unload polish model after` (default `Never`). Your next dictation loads the model again, so the first one may take a moment longer. `Immediately` frees it after about 10 seconds without a request.
- **Polish again with:** An Ollama model used for `Polish again with` is freed when nothing selects it (#4875).

### Fixes

- **Parakeet Ultra after updating (#4997, #5002):** After the 2.6.0 to 2.6.1 update, Parakeet could read as missing for people whose only Parakeet copy was Ultra, and dictation was blocked. EnviousWispr now re-checks the model already on your Mac at launch and uses it, with no new download.
- **Closing the main window (#4842, #4848):** Closing the main window (red button, Cmd+W or the Window menu) never quits EnviousWispr.
- **Whisper recovers after a decoding error (#4919, #4924):** Whisper reloads for the next dictation after the decoding error that could leave every later press failing.
- **Freezes:** Fixed freezes on the first keystroke in Settings search (#4778), on `Relaunch to apply` (#4801) and during disk space checks (#4917).
- **Crashes:** Custom word chips (#4760) and the learned-word checker warm-up (#4743).
- **Dictation:** A quick second press no longer loses a dictation (#4758); Parakeet loads right after a download that ends while the app runs (#4861); "3 o'clock" is written correctly (#4991, #4996); the comma after a spoken localhost port is kept (#4635, #4809).
- **Live Preview:** Live Preview works again on macOS 26 after Apple's speech helper restarts (#4937, #4938); `Auto` listens in your Mac's language, not the interface language (#4813, #4830); Mandarin stays Mandarin when your Mac's region differs (#4828, #4834).
- **History and Transcribe a File:** An open imported transcript keeps its playback position when the same original file is moved or relinked (#4808, #4832, #4831, #4854); if an import hits an unexpected error, Transcribe a File asks you to select the file again (#4756).
- **Pill and Settings:** New pills appear on the display of the active window (#4766); Hindi offers Whisper (#4448, #4763) and Greek recommends All Languages (#2615, #4815); date and time snippets use the Mac's language (#4824, #4835); Setup names the right System Settings path on macOS 27 (#4925); "model size" finds the EG-1 choice in Settings search (#4501, #4862).
- **Settings search privacy (#4843, #4853):** When EnviousWispr detects that a failed Settings search was dictated, it sends no words, and the words of a typed search longer than 6 words are not sent.
- **Narrow windows:** Toolbar controls on Snippets and on Dictionary's Your Words tab stay readable in a narrow Settings window (#4920).
- **Accessibility:** Search fields are named and small click areas are wider (#4545, #4807); import sheets and the meeting transcript respect Reduce Motion (#4866, #4876, #4869).
